draft.title: Fear of helot revolt
card: Helots were the enslaved workers who farmed the land for Spartan citizens. Most were Laconian or Messenian Greeks, and they greatly outnumbered the Spartans.
Spartans lived with the fear that helots would rise in revolt. A large Messenian revolt in the mid 600s BC and another around 465 BC showed that the fear had a real basis.
This fear helped to shape Spartan life. Citizens were trained as soldiers from boyhood so that they could keep control at home as well as fight abroad.

Control of helots was harsh. Each year the ephors declared war on the helots, which meant a Spartan could kill one without religious penalty. The krypteia, a group of young Spartans, was sent out to watch the countryside and kill helots seen as a threat.
draft.remember: Spartans were few and helots were many, so fear of revolt pushed Sparta towards military training and harsh control.

a.q: Why did Spartan citizens fear their helots?
opts: Helots greatly outnumbered them and might rise in revolt
Helots were trained as hoplites and could replace them
Helots refused to farm until they were given citizenship
Helots were allied with Athens and Thebes against Sparta
a.why: Helots were far more numerous than Spartans, and past revolts showed a rising was possible. The idea that helots were trained as hoplites is tempting, but the card describes them as farm workers, and the fear came from their numbers.
a.clue: Think about how the numbers of the two groups compared.

b.q: A historian argues that Sparta's military way of life was partly a response to the helots. Which point best supports this view?
opts: Citizens were trained as soldiers to keep control at home
Spartans fought in a phalanx, as many Greek cities did
Helots were given land in return for fighting for Sparta
Spartan women had more freedom than women elsewhere
b.why: Training every citizen as a soldier let a small group keep control over a much larger one, which links the army to the helot fear. The phalanx was used by many cities, so it does not show a response to helots in particular.
b.clue: Look for the answer that links Spartan training to keeping control at home.

a.best: Helots greatly outnumbered them and might rise in revolt

b.best: Citizens were trained as soldiers to keep control at home
